uncertainty.method: Per-pixel change in dB (after minus before) after 9x9 multilook in linear power, minus the median change of all measurable pixels (+0.23 dB for HH). The no-change spread sigma (1.01 dB) is 1.4826 x the median absolute deviation of the change. A pixel counts as changed when its change is at least k x sigma and at least 2 dB, for k = 2, 3 and 4; patches that cannot hold a disk 11 pixels across are removed. Pixels within 1.5 dB of the estimated noise floor on both dates are excluded as 'cannot tell'.
notes: Each area is a range, not one value: low uses the strict threshold (4 sigma), central 3 sigma and high the lenient one (2 sigma). The sensitivity list shows how other processing choices move the central value.
HH: 0% of the area is at or below the noise floor on 2026-09-27, 0% on 2026-10-21 and 0% on both.
HV: 1% of the area is at or below the noise floor on 2026-09-27, 0% on 2026-10-21 and 0% on both.
The noise floor is estimated from the darkest part of each image, not from the instrument's noise record. Pixels at the floor on only one date are kept; their change is a lower bound.
Changed patches narrower than about 110 m are not counted, so thin features such as narrow channels or roads are under-represented.

caveats.text: 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-21 are provisional-tier (calibrated, but values may change after reprocessing).
Wind roughens open water and changes its brightness from one pass to the next. A change over water is not by itself a change of the surface.
On steep slopes the radar image is distorted (layover) or blind (shadow); changes there are unreliable.
A change in radar brightness means the surface scatters the signal differently (water level, moisture, roughness, vegetation, structures). It is not by itself a land-cover label.

params.sigma_estimator: 1.4826 x median absolute deviation of the change
params.speck_removal: binary opening with a disk 11 pixels across

# Needs: pip install -e backend/  and an Earthdata Login in ~/.netrc (or EARTHDATA_TOKEN).
# Reads the best calibration tier available when it runs. This result used:
#   NISAR_L2_PR_GCOV_031_127_D_073_4005_DHDH_A_20260927T002830_20260927T002905_P05023_N_F_J_001 (provisional)
#   NISAR_L2_PR_GCOV_033_127_D_073_4005_DHDH_A_20261021T002830_20261021T002905_P05023_N_F_J_001 (provisional)
from nisar_investigator.schemas import ChangeRequest
from nisar_investigator.workflows.change import run_change

if __name__ == "__main__":  # required: the reader starts worker processes
    result = run_change(ChangeRequest(
        bbox=(-86.08, 30.37, -85.84, 30.49), date_before="2026-09-27", date_after="2026-10-21", track=127, polarization="HH",
    ))
    print(result.summary.headline)
    for m in result.summary.metrics:
        print(m.key, m.low, m.central, m.high, m.unit)

report.answer: Between 27 September and 21 October 2026, the floodplain showed radar brightness increased over 2.5 km² (0.05–32.4 km²) and decreased over 0.0–0.5 km². River gauges recorded water levels rising from 1.49 m to 3.31 m and 2.87 m to 3.56 m.
observed: Radar brightness rose over 2.48 km² (range 0.05–32.37 km²) and fell over 0.08 km² (range 0.0–0.5 km²) between 27 September and 21 October 2026. [chg_20261115_718fed94]
River gauges showed water levels rising from 1.49 m to 3.31 m (station 02366500) and 2.87 m to 3.56 m (station 02365769) during the same period. [ctx_river_gauges]
possible_explanations: The floodplain experienced flooding, causing increased water surface area and higher radar backscatter in HH polarization. To check: Compare with soil moisture data (SME2) or higher-resolution optical imagery to confirm surface water expansion.
Vegetation changes (e.g., inundation of vegetation) may explain the HV polarization decrease. To check: Analyze vegetation indices from optical satellites or field surveys.
unknown: The exact cause of the HV polarization decrease is not confirmed.
report.confidence: medium: Radar data shows significant brightness increase, and river gauges confirm rising water levels, but provisional calibration and wind effects on water surfaces introduce uncertainty.
